narrative.title: Carousel Alignment Check
narrative.scenario: A museum display carousel steps leftward one item at a time, and curators photograph its arrangement at random moments. An archivist must confirm whether a photographed arrangement is just the reference lineup after some number of steps — the same items, same cyclic order, different starting point. Different lengths or a genuinely different cyclic order mean the photo shows something else entirely.
narrative.inputFormat: Two strings s (the reference lineup) and goal (the photographed arrangement).
narrative.outputFormat: true when goal can be reached from s by repeatedly taking its first character and appending it to the end, false otherwise.
constraints: s and goal consist of lowercase English letters

testCases.explanation: Shifting a, b off the front and onto the back lands exactly on the photographed arrangement.
Same length, same letters, but no rotation reproduces the swapped tail.

hintLevels: Level 1: Every rotation of s is hiding inside s glued to itself — the doubled string is a ring unrolled onto a line.
Level 2: If the lengths differ, refuse immediately; otherwise concatenate s with itself and search for goal as a substring.
Level 3: Watch length equality separately — the doubled-string trick would happily find a short goal anywhere in s + s, so the length gate must come first.
